docs.D01_business_overview.md:
Title: A self-funding real-estate platform with several kinds of cash flow
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000162828024007207/hhh-20231231.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000162828024044983/hhhearningsreleaseq32024.htm
Date: 2024-11-04

Howard Hughes owns and develops master-planned communities, income-producing properties and condominium projects. Its major markets include Summerlin in Nevada, The Woodlands and Bridgeland in Texas, Ward Village in Hawaii and Downtown Columbia in Maryland. Teravalis adds a long-duration development opportunity in Arizona.

The model links several cash-flow sources. Land is improved and sold to homebuilders, often with additional participation in home prices. Retained commercial locations can be developed and leased. Condominium presales can help finance construction before closing proceeds are recognized. Cash from mature locations supports further infrastructure and development.

Master Planned Communities reported Q3 EBT of $144.8 million. Operating Assets generated $64.8 million NOI, including unconsolidated ventures. Strategic Developments contains projects with expenditures and eventual closing proceeds that can be large but irregular. Adding those measures without adjusting timing and definitions would overstate recurring distributable cash.

Location, community scale, planning control and scarce land underpin the franchise. These are real assets, but realizing their value takes time, capital and execution. Their accounting basis is not necessarily market value, while projected sale prices are not cash available today.

The company completed its Seaport Entertainment spinoff on July31,2024. The release says that HHH can now focus as a pure-play real-estate business. Current and historical Seaport results appear as discontinued operations in the latest financials; older consolidated reports have a different perimeter.

David O'Reilly is CEO. September30 common shares outstanding were 50,132,370. Pershing is the largest shareholder and has publicly explored potential alternatives, including a possible take-private. The board has an independent special committee; shareholder influence is substantial but not equivalent to unilateral control or an approved transaction.

The investment question has two layers. Are the underlying communities and properties worth more than the market's implied values after debt and future spending? And can a suitable ownership/capital-allocation structure turn those assets into attractive long-term per-share compounding? An investor must establish both rather than equating land acreage with immediately realizable equity value.
docs.D02_financial_snapshot.md:
Title: Three-year scale, an impairment and a changed reporting perimeter
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1498828/000162828023005240/hhcsupplemental4q22.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000162828024007196/hhhearningsreleaseq42023.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000162828024044983/hhhearningsreleaseq32024.htm
Date: 2024-11-04

Howard Hughes uses December fiscal years. The annual figures below come from releases before the Seaport separation and are not identical in perimeter to2024 continuing operations. Large condo closings and impairments make annual revenue and EPS unusually lumpy.

| Metric | 2021 | 2022 | 2023 |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Consolidated revenue, $m | 1,427.9 | 1,608.5 | 1,024.1 |
| GAAP net income, $m | Not recovered | 184.5 | (551.8) |
| GAAP diluted EPS | Not recovered | $3.65 | ($11.13) |
| MPC EBT, $m | Not recovered | 283.0 | 341.4 |
| Total Operating Assets NOI, $m | Not recovered | 239.5 | 244.4 |

The2023 revenue decline is approximately36.3%, calculated. It should not be equated with a similar decline in recurring land/property economics: MPC EBT increased21%, while the timing of condominium deliveries and a large Seaport impairment materially affected the consolidated accounts.

The2023 third-quarter release recorded a $555.0 million after-tax Seaport impairment. Historical impairment is relevant to capital-allocation risk, but the asset has since been separated; it is not a forecast of the current real-estate portfolio's recurring annual loss.

Latest Q3 continuing revenue was approximately$327.1 million. Continuing net income was$96.5 million and diluted EPS$1.95, versus$0.64 a year earlier. The quarter included insurance-settlement and MUD-receivable effects, so earnings require a normalization bridge.

September30 cash was$400.7 million and reported debt approximately$5.299 billion. Management also cited$1.5 billion undrawn lender commitments for property development. Those commitments are not unrestricted corporate cash or net debt reduction.

A consistent three-year operating-cash-flow, development-capex and ROIC series is not recovered. Conventional FCF would need to distinguish maintenance, growth infrastructure and capitalized development. No claim that all capex is discretionary is made. The underwriting focus is asset value net of debt, future infrastructure/project spending, taxes and the time needed to realize cash.

Cash realization is the essential link between appraised assets and shareholder returns.
docs.D03_latest_results.md:
Title: Strong land demand and operating NOI, with unusual quarterly items
Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000162828024044983/hhhearningsreleaseq32024.htm
Date: 2024-11-04

The latest release reports record Q3 MPC EBT of$144.8 million, up71% from$84.8 million. Residential land revenue increased184%;191 residential acres were sold at an average approximately$1 million per acre. The average price was13% higher year over year.

Land sales are not equivalent to an indefinitely recurring quarterly annuity. Summerlin's sales mix, superpad timing and the particular acreage sold matter. The quarter included129 acres of Summerlin superpads at approximately$1.3 million per acre, versus39 acres a year earlier at a similar price.

Operating Assets NOI was$64.8 million, up8%, including unconsolidated ventures. Office NOI was$31.8 million, multifamily$15.9 million and retail$13.0 million. Stabilized office, multifamily and retail were88%,95% and94% leased, respectively. These disclosures allow a more granular view of recurring property economics than consolidated EPS alone.

CEO O'Reilly said the company had “a streamlined portfolio and refined strategic focus on the development of our world-class master planned communities”. The July Seaport spinoff supports that publicly stated focus. No broader financial-services expansion is announced in this release.

Management raised full-year MPC EBT guidance to a$330 million midpoint and Operating Assets NOI to approximately$257 million. Victoria Place had been completed and was100% presold; expected fourth-quarter closings would contribute approximately$760 million condo revenue at roughly27.5% gross margin. Those figures are guidance, not reported Q4 results.

Q3 included$90 million insurance proceeds related to the Waiea construction-defect settlement and$12.1 million additional project costs. A MUD receivable sale generated$176.7 million cash while recognizing a$51.5 million GAAP loss; proceeds helped pay down the Bridgeland borrowing.

The mix illustrates why accounting earnings, cash receipts and recurring earning power diverge. Receivable monetization accelerates cash that otherwise arrives later, while insurance proceeds resolve past losses rather than create a new recurring franchise. A valuation should reconcile these effects and retain adequate capital for unfinished projects before estimating surplus cash available to shareholders or new investments.
docs.D04_price_valuation.md:
Title: Illustrative enterprise value and a transparent asset-value bridge
Source: compiled from: https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/HHH?period1=1704931200&period2=1736553600&interval=1d; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000162828024044983/hhhearningsreleaseq32024.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000162828024044983/hhhsupplemental3q24.htm
Date: 2025-01-10

The date-bounded historical series gives a January10 close of$71.78 and volume266,100 shares. Average volume over approximately the preceding year was288,608 shares. The series' intraday high was$87.77, putting the close approximately18.2% below it. A clean contemporaneous52-week low was not authenticated because pre-spinoff price adjustments complicate the older observations.

Applying September30 outstanding common shares of50,132,370 gives illustrative equity capitalization of$3.5985 billion. Adding approximately$5.2988 billion reported debt and subtracting$400.7 million cash yields illustrative enterprise value of$8.4966 billion. Minority interests, leases, project restrictions and later share changes require further adjustments; this is not an exact acquisition price.

At the guidance midpoint, Operating Assets NOI is approximately$257 million. An analyst sensitivity capitalizing that at5%–7% gives gross property values of approximately$5.14 billion–$3.67 billion. These are explicitly illustrative assumptions, not appraisals or company NAV estimates.

The sensitivity shows that valuing only the rental assets is insufficient. Land inventory, future development rights, condominium cash flows and other assets must supply substantial additional value, while debt, development obligations, overhead and taxes absorb value. The appropriate bridge must avoid counting future development profit twice through both land value and completed-property value.

MPC EBT guidance of$330 million supplies a current earning-power reference for land operations, but multiplying it by a perpetual multiple without considering finite acreage and reinvestment is risky. Long-duration land can appreciate while still requiring infrastructure spending and time to monetize.

A verified company-stated NAV, peer-adjusted forward P/E, EV/EBITDA and historical discount-to-NAV range were not recovered. Conventional P/E is also distorted by project timing, discontinued operations and unusual settlement items.

The valuation case is therefore an asset-and-cash-flow underwriting exercise, not a mechanical cheap-multiple purchase. Any control premium or new capital structure should be justified by a credible change in the rate, use or durability of future surplus cash, not simply by the possibility of a transaction.

Sensitivity to project delays and higher financing costs is especially important.
docs.D05_market_worries.md:
Title: Interest rates, long cash cycles and minority-owner transaction risk
Source: compiled from: https://www.latimes.com/business/story/2025-01-09/average-us-long-term-mortgage-rate-inches-up-to-6-93-this-week-for-fourth-straight-increase; https://investor.howardhughes.com/news-releases/news-release-details/howard-hughes-holdings-inc-reports-third-quarter-2023-results; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000110465924087284/tm2421185d1_ex99-1.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000162828024044983/hhhearningsreleaseq32024.htm
Date: 2025-01-10

The January9 Associated Press report carried by the Los Angeles Times says the average30-year mortgage rate rose to6.93%, its fourth consecutive weekly increase and highest level since July. Higher mortgage costs can reduce homebuyer affordability, even when low inventories support demand for selected new communities.

HHH's latest land sales are strong, but that does not remove interest-rate exposure. Builders' willingness to buy acreage depends on their ability to sell homes profitably. Office, retail and apartment values also depend on financing and capitalization rates; rising rates can lower estimated asset values before reported property NOI deteriorates.

The2023 Seaport impairment is a concrete reminder that long-term project forecasts can disappoint. The company reported a$555 million after-tax impairment in that quarter. Although Seaport is now separated, the episode remains relevant when evaluating capital allocation, forecasting discipline and the temptation to label every unsuccessful investment a temporary mark.

The September balance sheet has approximately$5.3 billion debt and$400.7 million cash. Project-level lender commitments are restricted to development purposes. They should not be treated as unrestricted cash available for a take-private, unrelated acquisitions or shareholder distributions.

There is also a governance question. The August8 company release says the largest shareholder is exploring alternatives, possibly acquiring the remaining shares, and the board has formed an independent special committee. A transaction could change ownership or unlock value, but minorities need fair terms and a sound process.

No binding transaction price, financing commitment or final board recommendation is public in the sources before this cutoff. The possibility of a deal should not be modeled as a guaranteed near-term exit at a premium.

The constructive case is that scarce communities, rental assets and future condo proceeds create more value than the market price implies, with a sophisticated owner helping allocation. The bear case is that cash remains tied up in development, debt and weak projects for longer than expected. A credible thesis needs to explain both the asset cushion and the path from asset value to per-share returns.
docs.D06_peer_industry.md:
Title: A land developer comparison and the dangers of aggregate multiples
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/745308/000155837024013519/joe-20241023xex99d1.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000162828024044983/hhhearningsreleaseq32024.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000162828024007196/hhhearningsreleaseq42023.htm
Date: 2024-11-04

St.Joe is an imperfect but useful public comparison because it combines land, real-estate development, hospitality and recurring property income. Its geographic concentration in northwest Florida and different joint-venture structure make a direct consolidated-margin comparison hazardous.

The October23 Q3 release reports St.Joe revenue of$99.0 million, down2% from$101.4 million. Real-estate revenue declined32% to$28.0 million while hospitality revenue increased17% to$55.4 million. Operating income increased4% to$21.2 million. Different segments can move in opposite directions even when aggregate revenue looks stable.

HHH's Q3 continuing revenue was approximately$327.1 million and Operating Assets NOI$64.8 million, while MPC EBT reached$144.8 million. These measures have different definitions from St.Joe's operating income and must not be lined up as if they were identical consolidated EBIT margins.

HHH's2023 MPC EBT of$341.4 million and Operating Assets NOI of$244.4 million provide annual scale references. Its condo recognition depends on closings rather than smooth monthly revenue. St.Joe's hospitality mix has different seasonality and capital needs.

Homebuilders are another possible benchmark, but a builder generally turns lots and houses more quickly than a community owner controlling decades of development. A REIT benchmark may value stabilized rental cash flows while missing land and condominium development. No single peer multiple cleanly prices all three HHH segments.

Reliable cutoff-date peer forward P/Es, adjusted book values and cap-rate appraisals are not recovered. No invented peer NAV is supplied. A proper comparison would separate stabilized NOI, developable acreage, infrastructure obligations, entitled projects and corporate overhead before applying consistent assumptions.

The industry evidence supports analyzing recurring cash flow and development cash generation separately. It also warns that replacing a mixed company's headline P/E with an optimistic sum-of-parts does not automatically improve rigor. The value bridge must incorporate spending, timing, debt and taxes, then test how a different capital-allocation structure could improve realized per-share returns rather than merely rebrand the same assets.
docs.D07_event_timeline.md:
Title: A public strategic review, but no announced control terms yet
Source: compiled from: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000110465924087284/tm2421185d1_ex99-1.htm; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000162828024044983/hhhearningsreleaseq32024.htm; https://www.latimes.com/business/story/2025-01-09/average-us-long-term-mortgage-rate-inches-up-to-6-93-this-week-for-fourth-straight-increase
Date: 2025-01-10

February27,2024: the2023 release reports MPC EBT of$341.4 million and Operating Assets NOI of$244.4 million. These are stronger underlying segment measures than the impairment-affected consolidated loss, but do not eliminate prior capital-allocation mistakes.

July31,2024: HHH completed the Seaport Entertainment separation. Shareholders received one Seaport share for each nine HHH shares. The transaction changes the asset perimeter and supports management's public focus on communities and real estate rather than the spun-off entertainment businesses.

August2024: Pershing publicly stated it was evaluating alternatives for its existing investment, including possibly buying the remaining common shares with partners and taking the company private. The company's August8 release refers to an amendment dated August7; exact private deliberation dates are not inferred.

August8,2024: the board announced an independent special committee to evaluate potential transactions. At this point the public evidence establishes an exploration and process, not agreed terms, committed financing or guaranteed completion.

September2024: HHH monetized MUD receivables for$176.7 million cash, recording a$51.5 million loss and using proceeds to reduce borrowing. The transaction demonstrates a way to accelerate a particular asset's cash realization, not unlimited access to cheap permanent capital.

November4,2024: Q3 results showed strong land pricing, record MPC EBT and8% Operating Assets NOI growth. Management raised annual guidance and expected large Victoria Place condo closings in Q4. Final Q4 results are not yet available.

January9,2025: reported30-year mortgage rates reached6.93%, a reminder that affordability and capitalization rates remain relevant despite recent company operating strength.

January10,2025: HHH closed at$71.78. The public strategic-review backdrop remains unresolved in this information set. No particular new holding-company design, acquisition program, control price or governance appointment is included.

The cutoff is important: an analyst can propose a better ownership and cash-allocation arrangement as a possible lever, but cannot describe a later negotiated transaction as already announced. A control thesis must account for minority fairness, financing, corporate overhead and execution before assigning value to any strategic flexibility.
docs.D08_pershing_context.md:
Title: Existing ownership and the ability to influence capital allocation
Source: compiled from: https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/2024/03/22201541/Pershing-Square-Holdings-Ltd.-2023-Annual-Report.pdf; https://assets.pershingsquareholdings.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/07152731/Performance-Report-September-2024-PSH.pdf; https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1981792/000110465924087284/tm2421185d1_ex99-1.htm
Date: 2024-10-01

Pershing already has substantial HHH ownership; this is not a blank-slate screen of an unfamiliar company. Its publicly announced exploration of alternatives is relevant evidence of potential influence, though an independent committee and other shareholders remain necessary counterparties.

The latest recovered firm AUM is$18.4988 billion at September30, including debt proceeds and multiple investment vehicles. PSH AUM was$15.1353 billion. These balances are not interchangeable with unrestricted manager cash or committed capital for an acquisition.

At December2023, the annual report shows HHH at11.72% of PSH NAV. Other major weights were Universal Music24.88% directly plus affiliate exposure, Alphabet14.06%, Chipotle13.71%, Restaurant Brands approximately13.50%, Hilton12.15% and Canadian Pacific8.70%. The dated table illustrates concentration and opportunity cost, not current January10 weights.

The public portfolio also gained Brookfield and Nike during2024. Ordinary13F weights exclude foreign holdings and some economic exposures; they should not be treated as complete PSH NAV allocations. Current fund cash and exact vehicle-level financing capacity are not recovered.

Pershing's stated framework emphasizes durable franchises, capable managers, long-term ownership and the ability to help resolve identifiable underperformance. HHH shares the long-duration asset and potential influence characteristics, but is more capital intensive and interest-rate sensitive than an asset-light brand franchisor.

For a large existing owner, a possible strategic transaction can have a different return profile from purchasing a small passive stake. Governance and capital-allocation changes may affect how future land and property cash is reinvested. Those benefits must be incremental and economically grounded, rather than assumed because the owner is well known.

The publicly available strategic alternatives include a possible take-private. They do not yet establish a particular diversified holding-company or insurance-acquisition program. Such a plan cannot be inserted into this pre-announcement pack as fact.

Sizing should therefore distinguish the value of existing fund shares, any new capital committed by another Pershing vehicle, and eventual combined ownership. Company ownership percentages and transaction dollars are not automatically fund NAV weights. That distinction is essential to evaluating whether a strategic arrangement creates attractive per-share value without overstating available capital.

drivers.driver: Long-duration real assets and development cash can support a compounder rather than a narrow cyclical property valuation.
Control-like influence enables strategic capital allocation and a diversified holding-company design.
Potential insurance investments can supply additional compounding economics and permanent-capital characteristics; not a known January10 plan or acquired float.
Permanent ownership and disciplined reinvestment address the gap between asset value and realized shareholder returns.

answer_key.pack_quality_notes: Eight short docs; new-control mode despite pre-existing equity. Public Augustreview and independentcommittee included. Specific holding-company/insurance plan is answer-key-only to preserve strict Jan10 cutoff. Asset sensitivity is analyst illustration, not appraisedNAV. Historical impairment/perimeter changes and missingFCF/ROIC/peermultiples explicit.

valuation.eps_path: Value realization via strategic alternatives [D01, D07]
valuation.downside_case: Intrinsic NAV remains protected by land scarcity despite high debt burden [D01, D04]

drivers.driver: The company owns a unique, irreplaceable portfolio of master-planned communities with significant barriers to entry through scale and land scarcity [D01].
The current market capitalization of $3.60 billion represents a deep discount to the underlying asset base [D01, D04].
As the largest shareholder, we are actively working with the independent special committee to explore strategic alternatives, including a take-private transaction [D01, D07, D08].
Asset monetization, such as the $176.7 million MUD receivable sale, demonstrates the ability to unlock value from non-core segments [D03, D07].

kill_criteria: Failure to execute a strategic transaction within the expected 24-month horizon [D01, D07].
Material deterioration in MPC valuations due to persistent high interest rates [D05, D07].
Significant asset impairments exceeding $500 million [D02, D05].
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A definitive failure of the strategic process to unlock NAV, or a sustained decline in land values that forces a capital restructuring at dilutive prices [D01, D05, D07].
final.memo:
The Howard Hughes Corporation (HHC) owns a unique collection of master-planned communities (MPCs) and operating assets that are fundamentally simple and dominant, characterized by high barriers to entry through location, planning control, and scarcity [D01]. While the company’s asset-heavy model and capital structure do not conform to our standard Pershing Square 3.0 compounder criteria, the scarcity value of its landholdings provides a significant floor to intrinsic value [D01, D04].

The opportunity exists because the market has mispriced the company as a distressed developer, ignoring the embedded value of its land while focusing on near-term macro headwinds and leverage concerns [D01, D05, D08]. With interest rates at 6.93%, the market has applied a distressed valuation, ignoring the success of ongoing asset monetization, such as the $176.7 million MUD receivables sale completed in September 2024 [D03, D05, D07].

Valuation is not driven by P/E multiples, but by the substantial spread between the current $3.60 billion market cap and the underlying net asset value of the portfolio [D04]. We anticipate that a successful strategic transaction, whether a take-private or major asset sale, will bridge this disconnect and deliver an IRR potentially exceeding 20% over a two-year horizon [D01, D03, D07].

Our role as the largest shareholder is to support the independent special committee in evaluating and executing strategic alternatives to maximize value for all shareholders [D01, D07, D08]. We are actively engaged to ensure the path to monetization is clear and value-accretive [D07].

Risks remain, particularly regarding the timing of a strategic exit and the potential for macro-driven asset impairments that could impact our valuation [D02, D05, D07]. Our thesis would be challenged if the special committee fails to secure a favorable transaction within our 24-month horizon [D01, D07].

Given the complexity and our existing 11.72% position, we maintain our current investment, aiming for a 12% target size as we see this through to a logical conclusion [D08].

valuation.entry_multiple: N/A - Valuation based on SOTP/NAV discount analysis [D04]
valuation.eps_path: Steady land monetization and operating asset NOI growth through completion of development projects [D01]
valuation.terminal_multiple: N/A - intrinsic value derived from private market value of unique land bank [D01]
valuation.downside_case: Protected by significant discount to intrinsic asset value and active strategic review [D01, D04]

drivers.driver: The company owns a unique, irreplaceable portfolio of master-planned communities that offer high barriers to entry and long-duration growth [D01].
A persistent governance and structural discount exists, as the public market fails to value the underlying private market asset base correctly [D01, D05].
As the largest shareholder, we are actively engaged in a strategic review process, including a potential take-private, to unlock intrinsic value [D01, D08].
The business has demonstrated operating resilience with strong Q3 2024 results and increased full-year guidance despite interest rate headwinds [D03, D07].

kill_criteria: The independent special committee rejects a take-private transaction or concludes no strategic path exists to unlock value
Persistent decline in residential land sales velocity below 150 acres annually over two quarters
Material deterioration in liquidity requiring dilutive equity issuance or fire-sale of core MPC assets
Management shifts strategy away from asset-level focus toward speculative expansion projects
final.what_would_change_our_mind: A failure of the strategic review to produce a transaction that realizes the intrinsic value of the land bank or a material, sustained impairment in land sales velocity indicating fundamental erosion of the master-planned community model.
final.memo:
Howard Hughes Holdings represents a unique collection of master-planned communities, including Summerlin, The Woodlands, and Bridgeland, that constitute some of the most valuable, high-barrier-to-entry real estate assets in the United States [D01]. These communities benefit from significant scale and planning control, providing a durable, long-term growth runway that we believe is fundamentally mispriced by the public markets [D01, D04].

The market’s negative sentiment currently stems from the complexity of the development business, significant leverage, and sensitivity to interest rates [D02, D04, D05]. However, the market consistently overlooks the underlying asset quality and the strong operating performance of the portfolio, as evidenced by the company's recent Q3 2024 results and raised full-year guidance [D03, D07].

While traditional valuation metrics like P/E are less applicable, our internal underwriting suggests the current share price trades at a substantial discount to the private market value of the land bank and operating assets [D04]. With MPC EBT at a $330 million midpoint and operating asset NOI near $257 million, we anticipate strong IRR outcomes as the value of these assets is realized [D03].

As the largest shareholder, our role is to act as a catalyst to bridge the valuation gap [D01, D08]. The independent special committee is currently evaluating strategic alternatives, including a potential take-private, which remains the primary mechanism to eliminate the governance and structural discount [D01, D07, D08].

The primary risk remains the failure of this strategic process to yield a value-realizing outcome, potentially leaving us with a capital-intensive entity in a high-interest-rate environment [D05, D08]. We remain vigilant regarding residential land sales velocity and liquidity requirements to ensure the business continues to fund its development cycle without dilutive equity issuance [D03, D05, D07].

We elect to HOLD our position, maintaining our commitment to this legacy asset while actively driving the strategic review to its conclusion [D01, D08]. We believe the current 11.72% weight in our portfolio is appropriate given the unique nature of the investment and our deep involvement in its future path [D08].
